body.decision: Use Claude Code as the only conversational agent. SQL Investigator is a local .NET MCP stdio process that Claude Code launches; there is no separate web UI, chat application or embedded local model.
body.rationale: A standalone chat application, web service or embedded LLM adds operational and security surfaces without improving the investigation workflow.
body.title: Claude Code as sole agent host

body.decision: Support only SQL Server and T-SQL, using Microsoft.Data.SqlClient for access and Microsoft.SqlServer.TransactSql.ScriptDom for validation.
body.rationale: A generic database provider abstraction would dilute the grammar-specific safety guarantees the validator relies on.
body.title: SQL Server and T-SQL only

consequences: Reject unsupported AST forms, writes, multiple batches, unsafe references and excessive work before execution.
Use dedicated read-only SQL principals as the final write barrier, and keep evidence logs.
body.decision: Allow Claude Code to run multiple SELECT investigations without per-query human approval, only within independent, fail-closed MCP-side and SQL Server-side policy boundaries.
body.rationale: Per-SELECT human approval breaks the intended conversational workflow; trusting the model to police itself is unsafe, so enforcement must be independent of the agent.
body.title: Bounded autonomous read-only investigation

consequences: Each store has exactly one writing service; files use current-user-only ACLs; recovery is tested; logs are secret-redacted.
body.decision: Use System.Text.Json files with atomic replacement for connection metadata, knowledge and history; protect credentials separately with Windows DPAPI CurrentUser.
body.rationale: SQLite adds a database dependency that a single-user local tool does not need; plaintext credentials are unacceptable.
body.title: Local JSON and DPAPI, not SQLite

consequences: Provenance is preserved per database; unverified relationships are proposed, never asserted.
body.decision: Query each authorized database independently through its own alias; Claude Code correlates the bounded observations and reports unmatched and ambiguous matches.
body.rationale: Linked servers and cross-database server-side joins broaden privileges and create hidden coupling between independently authorized databases.
body.title: Separate queries and agent-side correlation

body.decision: Use Continuum for architecture governance and the implementation handoff only. Optional exported context files may be imported as knowledge, but the executable has no Continuum runtime dependency.
body.rationale: A runtime dependency would complicate a small local investigation tool and tie it to a networked service.
body.title: Continuum at design time, optional knowledge at runtime

Bindings: os-user-secret-store replaces windows-dpapi-currentuser; LocalMCPServer bound for windows-x64 osx-arm64 osx-x64; acceptance step credential.dpapi-current-user becomes credential.user-protected
Production macOS distribution requires Developer ID signing and notarization; until then macOS builds are development builds
body.decision: Support win-x64, osx-arm64 and osx-x64 (macOS 15 or later) as one product. Keep System.Text.Json files with atomic replacement and one writing service per store, and no SQLite. Protect each alias's credential with the OS per-user secret store: DPAPI CurrentUser on Windows, unchanged; one application-scoped generic-password item per alias in the login Keychain on macOS, created and deleted only by the local console. Owner-only data folders on both (NTFS DACLs; 0700/0600). Fail closed with credential.unavailable, never prompt or downgrade, when the Keychain refuses. Supersedes ADR-004 (its store decision is restated unchanged).

options.name: macos
options.summary: Run SQL Investigator on macOS as well as Windows. Only descriptions change: the deployable, the environment, the credential vault and the provisioning test no longer name Windows or DPAPI, because the operating-system mechanism is a technology choice and lives in the binding. No element, edge, owner or constraint is added, removed or moved: the vault is still a secret-store no service writes, and secrets still enter only at the local console. Draft for ADR-007; not proposed.

body.rationale: macOS developers cannot use a Windows-only tool. Everything but credential protection, owner-only permissions and the data path is already cross-platform. Each OS's own per-user store keeps secrets out of plaintext without a passphrase the unattended server would have to hold.
risks: Unsigned or ad-hoc builds are identified by code hash, so every update re-prompts for Keychain access or needs re-provisioning
GitHub macOS runners cannot host SQL Server; macOS SQL connectivity needs a reachable test server
body.title: Support macOS; protect credentials with the operating system's per-user secret store
